1→# Architecture
   2→
   3→This document explains the system to someone who has read the README and has five minutes.
   4→Every claim here describes the code as it stands; nothing is planned or partial except where
   5→the Limits section says so plainly.
   6→
   7→## Overview
   8→
   9→Ryde is a multi-agent dispute resolution system for ride-hailing: a party files a dispute
  10→through a web intake form, and the system resolves the two categories it handles — route
  11→deviation and no-show charge — end to end. Three agents do the work: a Rider Advocate and a
  12→Driver Advocate each build their side's case from the evidence, and a Judge weighs both
  13→cases, applies company policy and issues a ruling with a confidence score. Every computed
  14→figure the agents argue from comes from a deterministic Evidence Pack calculated in Python
  15→before any model is called; agents cite pack fields by reference and are forbidden from
  16→doing their own arithmetic, and the only other number they see is the amount the party
  17→asked for. The decisions that must never depend on a model's obedience — the confidence
  18→threshold, the SGD 50 autonomous cap, the requirement that a route ruling rest on a measured
  19→deviation, the two money gates NS-6 and RD-5, the one-round follow-up limit, and the routing of
  20→out-of-scope categories to human review — are enforced in Python code, not asked of the model in
  21→a prompt. The system
  22→has two surfaces: an operator console that shows the full case file and the agent-to-agent
  23→traffic, and a party page where the filing party submits the form and reads only what they
  24→are allowed to read.
  25→
  26→## Diagram
  27→
  28→The whole system on one page. A dispute arrives either through the web intake form or the
  29→command-line runner; the two swappable inputs (the policy document and the dataset pack)
  30→enter from the side. Every step of a run lands in the event log, and the operator console
  31→renders the event strip embedded in the case file — opening each event's full payload from
  32→the run files the operator attaches.
  33→
  34→```mermaid
  35→flowchart TD
  36→    PACK["Dataset pack"] --> B["Server"]
  37→    PACK --> CL["Command-line runner"]
  38→    A["Rider intake form"] --> B
  39→    B --> C{"Category in scope?"}
  40→    CL --> C
  41→    C -- "Out of scope" --> H["Human review"]
  42→    C -- "Route deviation or no-show" --> E["Evidence Pack"]
  43→    POL["Policy document"] --> RA["Rider Advocate"]
  44→    POL --> DA["Driver Advocate"]
  45→    POL --> J["Judge"]
  46→    E --> RA
  47→    E --> DA
  48→    RA --> S{"Questions for the party?"}
  49→    DA --> S
  50→    S -- "Yes, first round" --> O4["Needs info"]
  51→    O4 --> PA["Party answers follow-ups"]
  52→    PA -- "Fresh run with the answers" --> B
  53→    S -- "No" --> J
  54→    J --> G{"Gates pass? Confidence, cap, measured deviation, NS-6, RD-5"}
  55→    G -- "Yes" --> O1["Ruled"]
  56→    G -- "No" --> O2["Withheld"]
  57→    O2 -- "Candidate ruling queued" --> H
  58→    J -- "Model could not answer" --> H
  59→    B -. "Every step emits an event" .-> L["Event log"]
  60→    J -.-> L
  61→    L -- "Embedded in the case file" --> K["Operator console"]
  62→```
  63→
  64→## Components
  65→
  66→| Component | File(s) | Responsibility |
  67→|---|---|---|
  68→| Pipeline | `app/pipeline.py` | Runs one dispute end to end, moves the case between agents, records every step |
  69→| Dispute record and routing | `app/dispute.py` | Parses the two record shapes, normalises categories, routes out-of-scope filings away |
  70→| Evidence layer | `app/evidence/compute.py` | Computes the Evidence Pack by plain arithmetic; a missing input inside a record becomes a null with a note, never a guess — a number that is present but **not a finite number** (NaN or Infinity, which a JSON reader accepts, or an **integer too large** for a float) counts as missing, and it voids what it feeds rather than being dropped from a formula. A figure the layer's own arithmetic would **overflow** into (a huge distance over a tiny estimate) is missing too, never Infinity. An **impossible** input — a negative rate, a surge of zero or less, or a promo larger than the fare — voids the fare the same way, with a note and an entry in `fare.unreadable_inputs`. A route case with no trip record, or a no-show case with no cancellation record, aborts the run before any pack is built |
  71→| Agent scaffolding | `app/agents/base.py` | Shared prompts, the LLM call, and citation validation against the pack and the policy |
  72→| Rider Advocate | `app/agents/rider_advocate.py` | Argues the rider's side from the pack and the policy |
  73→| Driver Advocate | `app/agents/driver_advocate.py` | Argues the driver's side from the pack and the policy |
  74→| Judge | `app/agents/judge.py` | Weighs both cases, issues one ruling, withholds it behind the gates |
  75→| Event log | `app/events.py` | The append-only record of who said what to whom, with full payloads on disk |
  76→| Output contracts | `app/schemas.py` | The typed shapes agents must produce; builds the party-facing decision message |
  77→| Policy loader | `app/policy.py` | Reads the policy document, extracts rule IDs, fails loudly when it is missing |
  78→| Mock LLM | `app/llm/mock.py` | Deterministic stand-in provider; its free-text fields — claim summaries, arguments, the Judge's explanation — carry a `MOCK` prefix, while actions, rule IDs and evidence refs do not |
  79→| Tencent adapter | `app/llm/tencent.py` | The real provider: calls one Tencent Cloud ADP app per agent over HTTP |
  80→| HTTP server | `app/server.py` | The intake API, the party view allowlist, and static files for both pages |
  81→| Command-line runner | `app/cli.py` | Runs one dispute from the terminal and prints the event strip |
  82→| Runtime configuration | `app/config.json` | Confidence threshold, autonomous cap, default dataset pack, provider settings |
  83→| Operator console | `ui/app.js` | Renders the case file: grievance, evidence, both claims, resolution, event strip |
  84→| Party page | `ui/party/party.js` | The intake form and the outcome view the filing party sees |
  85→| Policy document | `docs/policy.md` | The rule set the agents cite, with per-rule provenance |
  86→
  87→## Lifecycle of a dispute
  88→
  89→`run_dispute` in `app/pipeline.py` walks one dispute through these steps, in this order,
  90→emitting an event at each:
  91→
  92→1. `run.started` — the system records the dispute id, category, LLM provider, confidence
  93→   threshold and the policy rule IDs in force.
  94→2. `dispute.filed` — the raw intake-form submission is logged exactly as it arrived.
  95→3. **Routing.** If the category is outside the two handled ones, the run emits
  96→   `dispute.routed_to_human_review`, then `party.notified` with the neutral support message,
  97→   then `run.completed` — and no agent runs at all.
  98→4. `evidence.pack_built` — the Evidence Pack is computed in Python, before any LLM call,
  99→   and offered to the agents as the source of every computed figure — the only other
 100→   number they see is the amount the party claimed.
 101→5. `case.assigned` — once to each advocate.
 102→6. Each advocate runs and emits `advocate.case_submitted` to the Judge with its case. When
 103→   an advocate needs more from the filing party, it selects offered slot IDs and emits
 104→   `advocate.follow_up_requested` in the first round with both the selected slots and the
 105→   rendered questions. Code renders a bank sentence for a rider-filed dispute, or a form
 106→   sentence from an intake label for either filer; any question text written by the model
 107→   is ignored. The party-safety check remains a backstop, and only rendered questions that
 108→   pass it reach the party.
 109→7. **Stop and ask.** If there are questions to send and the dispute does not already carry
 110→   the party's answers, the run stops before the Judge: `party.notified` carries the
 111→   rendered questions — or, when none survive the backstop, plain template questions the
 112→   pipeline builds for blank intake fields — then `run.completed` records the `needs_info`
 113→   outcome. The party's answers start a fresh run, which is guaranteed to reach the Judge.
 114→8. `judge.deliberation_started` — both cases are handed to the Judge together.
 115→9. The Judge rules: `judge.ruling_issued` when every gate passes, or
 116→   `judge.ruling_withheld` when one fails — the candidate ruling is recorded either way.
 117→10. `party.notified` — the message the parties actually receive, as opposed to what was
 118→    decided internally.
 119→11. `run.completed` — the outcome is recorded and the case file is written.
 120→
 121→## The four outcomes
 122→
 123→| Outcome | When it happens | Did the Judge run? | Party page shows |
 124→|---|---|---|---|
 125→| `ruled` | The Judge issued a ruling and every gate passed | Yes | `decided` |
 126→| `withheld` | A gate stopped the ruling, or the model could not answer after its allowed retries | Yes for a gate — the candidate is recorded for a human reviewer, never delivered; no candidate exists for a model failure | `under_review` |
 127→| `human_review` | The category is outside the two the agents handle | No — routed away before any agent | `passed_to_support` |
 128→| `needs_info` | The advocates selected offered follow-up slots in the first round, or a blank form answer produced a template question | No — the run stops before the Judge | `needs_info` |
 129→
 130→## Gates enforced in code
 131→
 132→Eight gates stand between a filing and a ruling, and each is enforced in Python, not asked of
 133→the model in a prompt:
 134→
 135→| Gate | File | Condition as written in code |
 136→|---|---|---|
 137→| Confidence threshold | `app/agents/judge.py` | `ruling.confidence < confidence_threshold` — the threshold is 0.65, read from `app/config.json` |
 138→| ESC-4, the autonomous cap | `app/agents/judge.py` | A money ruling whose `recommended_amount_sgd` exceeds the cap is withheld; the cap is SGD 50 from `app/config.json` |
 139→| ESC-2, unmeasured deviation, unproven charge or unreadable fare input | `app/agents/judge.py` | On a route-deviation case, the ruling is withheld when `route.deviation_pct` is not a recorded finite figure, when `fare.charged_sgd` is not one (or the fare block is absent), or when the record states a fare input it cannot read (`fare.unreadable_inputs` non-empty: a broken tariff rate or promo) — EV-1 names the deviation and the fare charged as the figures a fare finding needs, and a figure the record cannot prove is a missing figure |
 140→| NS-6, contested no-show | `app/agents/judge.py` | On a no-show case where the driver marked a no-show, the rider claims the driver was absent, and `cancellation.driver_distance_from_pickup_m` is null, the fee has no GPS proof: a refund is issued automatically only when the fee is at most SGD 10 and the rider's `fraud_flags` are recorded and zero with no more than half of past disputes rejected; any other ruling is withheld, and the refund must equal the fee to the cent |
 141→| RD-5, proven overcharge | `app/agents/judge.py` | On a route-deviation case where `fare.difference_sgd` is recorded and at least SGD 1.00, a ruling that refunds less than the proven difference is withheld |
 142→| One-round follow-up limit | `app/pipeline.py` | `if questions and not dispute.follow_up_answers` — a dispute is asked at most once; with answers present the Judge always runs and fresh questions are recorded but not sent |
 143→| Out-of-scope routing | `app/pipeline.py` | `if not dispute.is_agent_handled` — anything outside route deviation and no-show charge goes to human review before any agent runs; an unrecognised category normalises to "other" in `app/dispute.py` |
 144→| Answer once | `app/server.py` | The answers route claims the run with an exclusive create (`O_CREAT \| O_EXCL`) before re-running it — a `needs_info` run can be answered exactly once and cannot produce two rulings |
 145→
 146→Why in code? Because a prompt is a request — a model can misread it, and there is no
 147→recourse when it does. Code is a guarantee: the branch either runs or it does not, and the
 148→event log shows which. ESC-4 in particular moves money, so it must not depend on the LLM
 149→having read its instructions carefully.
 150→
 151→## Observability
 152→
 153→Every run writes three things under `runs/<run_id>/`:
 154→
 155→- `events.jsonl` — one JSON line per event, append-only, never rewritten: who sent what to
 156→  whom, when, with a one-line summary.
 157→- `payloads/` — the full payload behind each event, named by sequence number and event
 158→  type, so the strip stays readable and the detail stays one click away.
 159→- `case_file.json` — the assembled record: what was claimed, the evidence pack, both
 160→  advocate cases, the resolution, and the event strip. Self-contained, so one file tells
 161→  the whole story of one run.
 162→
 163→A run filed through the server writes one more file: `dispute.json`, the record the pipeline
 164→actually ran on (the command-line runner does not write it). When a `needs_info` run is
 165→answered, its directory also gains `answered.json`, recording which run the answers
 166→produced.
 167→
 168→The operator console (`ui/app.js`) renders the case file: the event strip shows one row per
 169→event — sequence, time, sender to recipient, summary — and expanding a row opens the full
 170→payload from the run directory attached in the browser. Payload references are sanitised, so
 171→a console loaded with a hostile file can be pointed at nothing outside the run. The
 172→command-line runner prints the same strip to the terminal.
 173→
 174→## What the parties see
 175→
 176→`party_view` in `app/server.py` is an allowlist that fails closed. The party page is handed
 177→exactly five keys — run id, dispute id, status, message, questions — and any malformed case
 178→file degrades to the neutral under-review message with no questions. A withheld ruling's
 179→amount and the Judge's confidence are structurally absent from everything the party is
 180→sent, not merely unrendered. `party_message_for_ruling` in `app/schemas.py` composes the
 181→decision message in code from structured fields — the action, the amount, and the plain
 182→titles of the policy rules cited — and the Judge's explanation never crosses this boundary:
 183→it stays in the operator console. Every non-decision status shows a canonical constant
 184→message, whatever a stale or planted case file might say. The two kinds of party-facing text
 185→are protected differently. The decision message is composed in code from structured fields,
 186→so nothing model-written reaches it: it names the action and the amount — a no-action ruling
 187→carries no amount — and at most three rule titles, never the escalation (ESC) rules. On a
 188→decided view the message leads with a demo notice whenever the ruling's LLM record does not
 189→prove the real provider — only a record that is a non-array dict whose provider field is
 190→exactly `tencent` suppresses it, and any other record, missing, mock or malformed, keeps it —
 191→so a decision made on an illustrative run never reads like a live review, while a proven
 192→real-provider decision shows no notice.
 193→Follow-up questions are selected by the advocates as slot IDs; code renders each sentence
 194→from the fixed category bank or from an intake form label. Bank slots are offered only when
 195→the rider filed, while form slots work for either filer. Any question text written by the
 196→model is ignored, so no model-written text reaches a party. The word check (`is_party_safe`,
 197→applied in `_questions_for_party` in `app/pipeline.py` and again in `party_view`) remains a
 198→backstop, as it is for the code-composed decision message. When no rendered question survives,
 199→the pipeline falls back to plain template questions built from the form's own labels. A run
 200→that asked for more information is answered through `POST /api/disputes/<run_id>/answers`, and
 201→the answers start a fresh run on the same dispute.
 202→
 203→## Policy and dataset packs
 204→
 205→`docs/policy.md` is data, not code: rules with IDs (GEN, EV, RD, NS, ESC families),
 206→preconditions written against pack fields in plain language, and per-rule provenance
 207→stating whether a rule comes from Ryde's own published policy, a comparable operator, or
 208→the project team. The pipeline reads it at the path in `app/config.json`; a different
 209→policy document drops in with no code change. Nothing in the code evaluates the
 210→preconditions — the Judge reads the rules and applies them in its reasoning. Citing a rule
 211→that does not exist is recorded rather than blocked: an unknown ID is logged under the
 212→ruling's `validation.unknown_rule_ids` with a note and the ruling still issues, but only
 213→titles of rules the policy actually defines can reach the party message.
 214→
 215→Two dataset packs live under `data/packs/`: `organiser-style-v1` — the default in
 216→`app/config.json` — which holds the corpus in the organisers' record shape, including their
 217→own DISP-002 verbatim; and `ryde-synth-v1`, the same 17 cases in this project's own record
 218→shape. Swapping corpora is a directory copy, never a code change. Each pack carries a
 219→`ground-truth.json` of expected outcomes, kept out of what the agents see: the agents get
 220→the dispute record, the evidence pack and the policy — never the answer — so replayed-run
 221→consistency can be measured honestly.
 222→
 223→## LLM provider
 224→
 225→Agent logic never talks to a vendor SDK. Every agent builds a request and calls one seam:
 226→the `LLMClient` interface in `app/llm/`, a single `complete` method whose response carries
 227→the text plus provenance (provider, model, usage, finish reason). Two adapters implement
 228→it. The mock provider, `app/llm/mock.py`, returns deterministic contract-shaped responses,
 229→so the full pipeline runs with no API key and the same dispute always produces the same
 230→decisions and the same computed figures (the run id and the event timestamps differ from
 231→run to run). Its free-text fields — claim summaries, arguments, the Judge's explanation —
 232→carry a `MOCK` prefix, so a mock run can never be mistaken for a real ruling; actions, rule
 233→IDs and evidence refs are not prefixed. The party decision message, composed in code, is
 234→marked differently: on a decided party view it leads with a fixed demo notice stating that
 235→the decision came from an illustrative run and is not a live review, shown whenever the
 236→ruling's LLM record does not prove the Tencent provider, and only a record whose provider
 237→field is exactly `tencent` shows a decision with no notice. The Tencent adapter,
 238→`app/llm/tencent.py`, implements the same interface over Tencent Cloud ADP (Agent
 239→Development Platform). Each agent is its own published ADP app with its own key: Rider
 240→Advocate, Driver Advocate and Judge. The apps carry only a short role card; the adapter
 241→sends the full role prompt on every call, so the prompts live in this repo and every gate
 242→stays in Python. Three things about the endpoint shape the adapter. Tencent's web firewall
 243→blocks prompts that mix backticks with ASCII brackets, so the adapter drops backticks and
 244→sends full-width brackets, which the model reads the same way; a blocked call is classified
 245→as permanent and is never asked again. ADP reports errors inside a successful HTTP response,
 246→so the adapter reads every event rather than trusting the status code. The free plan allows
 247→10 calls a minute, so calls are spaced at least 6.5 seconds apart. The agent layer retries a
 248→transient failure up to three times, with waits of 2, 5 and 10 seconds; a contract failure
 249→is asked again once. A parsed reply is final: a low confidence or capped ruling is never
 250→asked again. One case shares a 120 seconds time budget from `llm.case_budget_seconds`; each
 251→retry is recorded as `llm.call_retried`. When the budget cannot cover a call or wait, or the
 252→model still cannot answer, the pipeline returns a withheld case and emits
 253→`dispute.escalated_on_model_failure`; the case file keeps the `model_failure` record for the
 254→reviewer. There is no silent fallback to the mock. The mock stays the default provider, so
 255→the tests and a fresh checkout need no keys; `--llm tencent` selects the real model.
 256→
 257→## Limits
 258→
 259→What the system does not do yet, stated plainly:
 260→
 261→- **A failed model call is escalated.** The party waits while retries run and sees the neutral
 262→  under-review message; after the case is queued for human review, the party is not notified later.
 263→- **Amounts must come back as JSON numbers.** A model reply carrying an amount as a string
 264→  is rejected, never converted, because the value moves money.
 265→- **Two categories only.** Route deviation and no-show charge. Property damage and safety
 266→  incidents route to human review by design.
 267→- **The driver-side form is not built.** The party page files as the rider only; the
 268→  pipeline itself accepts driver-filed disputes, but no web form offers it yet.
 269→- **Follow-up wording is code-owned.** Advocates select slot IDs; code renders each question
 270→  from the fixed category bank or an intake form label, and model-written question text is
 271→  ignored. Bank slots are rider-only; form slots are available to either filer.
 272→- **The word check is a backstop.** Rendered follow-up questions and the code-composed decision
 273→  message pass the keyword gate, which is not a semantic guarantee; blank fields still use
 274→  template questions built from the form's own labels.
 275→- **Policy preconditions are not evaluated by code.** The rules are written against pack
 276→  fields in plain language; nothing checks them mechanically, and the Judge applies them by
 277→  reading them.
 278→

1→# Ryde — Multi-Agent Autonomous Dispute Resolution
   2→
   3→Entry for the **Tencent Cloud "AI CAN DO IT" Hackathon Singapore 2026**, Digital Native track
   4→(the Ryde challenge statement, section 5 of the organisers' document).
   5→
   6→**Status: the system runs end to end on the real Tencent Cloud model (ADP), with the
   7→deterministic mock as the default for a fresh checkout.** The scope is ruled: a two-category MVP
   8→(route deviation + no-show charge) with three agents, a deterministic evidence layer, and an
   9→observable case-file view. The challenge statement is in
  10→[`docs/statement-extract.md`](docs/statement-extract.md); the builder's contract is in
  11→[`CODEBUDDY.md`](CODEBUDDY.md).
  12→
  13→## The challenge
  14→
  15→Ride-hailing platforms process thousands of dispute tickets daily: fare disputes, route deviations,
  16→property damage, safety incidents, no-show charges. They are subjective, emotionally charged, and
  17→currently resolved by humans reviewing GPS telemetry, chat logs, payment records and company policy
  18→by hand. The result is slow, expensive and inconsistent.
  19→
  20→The task is an autonomous multi-agent system that gathers evidence, builds both sides' cases, applies
  21→company policy and issues a fair ruling with a confidence score and a plain-language explanation.
  22→
  23→## Architecture
  24→
  25→Three core agents, all MVP-required:
  26→
  27→| Agent | Role |
  28→|---|---|
  29→| **Rider Advocate** | Builds the rider's case from the Evidence Pack and the policy |
  30→| **Driver Advocate** | Builds the driver's case from the Evidence Pack and the policy |
  31→| **Judge** | Weighs both cases, applies policy, rules, and explains the reasoning with a confidence score |
  32→
  33→Inter-agent communication must be **observable** — a judge needs to see how the agents exchange
  34→information and build their cases. That surface is a required deliverable, not a nice-to-have.
  35→
  36→The full walkthrough — components, lifecycle, gates, observability — is in
  37→[`docs/architecture.md`](docs/architecture.md). The system on one page:
  38→
  39→```mermaid
  40→flowchart TD
  41→    PACK["Dataset pack"] --> B["Server"]
  42→    PACK --> CL["Command-line runner"]
  43→    A["Rider intake form"] --> B
  44→    B --> C{"Category in scope?"}
  45→    CL --> C
  46→    C -- "Out of scope" --> H["Human review"]
  47→    C -- "Route deviation or no-show" --> E["Evidence Pack"]
  48→    POL["Policy document"] --> RA["Rider Advocate"]
  49→    POL --> DA["Driver Advocate"]
  50→    POL --> J["Judge"]
  51→    E --> RA
  52→    E --> DA
  53→    RA --> S{"Questions for the party?"}
  54→    DA --> S
  55→    S -- "Yes, first round" --> O4["Needs info"]
  56→    O4 --> PA["Party answers follow-ups"]
  57→    PA -- "Fresh run with the answers" --> B
  58→    S -- "No" --> J
  59→    J --> G{"Gates pass? Confidence, cap, measured deviation, NS-6, RD-5"}
  60→    G -- "Yes" --> O1["Ruled"]
  61→    G -- "No" --> O2["Withheld"]
  62→    O2 -- "Candidate ruling queued" --> H
  63→    J -- "Model could not answer" --> H
  64→    B -. "Every step emits an event" .-> L["Event log"]
  65→    J -.-> L
  66→    L -- "Embedded in the case file" --> K["Operator console"]
  67→```
  68→
  69→## Documents
  70→
  71→- [`docs/statement-extract.md`](docs/statement-extract.md) — the challenge statement, verbatim
  72→- [`docs/architecture.md`](docs/architecture.md) — architecture diagram and system description
  73→- [`docs/policy.md`](docs/policy.md) — the policy rule set the Judge applies, with per-rule provenance
  74→- [`docs/dataset.md`](docs/dataset.md) — the labelled corpus, its provenance and its limitations
  75→- [`docs/evidence-plan.md`](docs/evidence-plan.md) — development-process evidence rules
  76→- [`CODEBUDDY.md`](CODEBUDDY.md) — builder's entry point and project memory
  77→
  78→## Development tooling
  79→
  80→Built with Tencent Cloud **CodeBuddy**. The competition mandates proof of product usage, so
  81→development happens in the tool and evidence is captured as it occurs.
  82→
  83→## Run
  84→
  85→No dependencies and no API key needed for a first look: it runs on a stock Python 3.9+ with the
  86→standard library only, using a deterministic mock in place of the LLM.
  87→
  88→```bash
  89→python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .
  90→python3 -m app.cli --pack ryde-synth-v1 --dispute RD-0101
  91→python3 -m app.cli --pack organiser-style-v1 --dispute DISP-002
  92→```
  93→
  94→The evaluation harness replays every labelled case — `python3 -m app.eval --llm tencent --repeat 3` —
  95→and scores the rulings against the labels, answering a round-one stop and running it again.
  96→
  97→`--dispute` takes either a dispute id inside the selected pack or a path to a record file
  98→(`python3 -m app.cli --dispute data/packs/ryde-synth-v1/disputes/RD-0101.json`). The pack
  99→defaults to `dataset_pack` in `app/config.json`; `--pack` overrides it for one run.
 100→
 101→That prints the agent-to-agent event strip and the ruling, and writes the run's artifacts to
 102→`runs/<run_id>/`: `events.jsonl` (the observable traffic), `payloads/*.json` (the full payload
 103→behind each event) and `case_file.json` (evidence, both claims, resolution).
 104→
 105→The corpus lives in two swappable packs under `data/packs/`: `ryde-synth-v1` (our 17 labelled
 106→cases, our record shape) and `organiser-style-v1` (the same 17 cases as twins in the organisers'
 107→shape, plus the organisers' own `DISP-002` verbatim). `RD-0103` is a deviation too small to
 108→matter, `NS-0203` is a driver who marked arrival 885 m from the pickup point, `RD-0109` is a
 109→remedy above the autonomous cap that the system refuses to issue on its own, and `OS-0301` is an
 110→out-of-scope filing routed to human review without an LLM call. `docs/dataset.md` maps each case
 111→to what it tests; `<pack>/ground-truth.json` holds the expected outcomes, deliberately kept out
 112→of the records the agents see.
 113→
 114→Five gates stand between a ruling and the parties, and **all five are enforced in Python, not
 115→asked of the model in a prompt**: the confidence threshold, ESC-4's SGD 50 autonomous cap, ESC-2,
 116→which withholds a route-case ruling when the deviation cannot be measured or the fare charged
 117→cannot be established, NS-6, which withholds a
 118→contested no-show unless the ruling is a refund of exactly the fee for a low fee and a clean rider
 119→record, and RD-5, which withholds a route ruling that refunds less than the overcharge the records
 120→prove. Each gate withholds the ruling for a human; none of them rewrites what the Judge proposed.
 121→Try them:
 122→
 123→```bash
 124→python3 -m app.cli --pack ryde-synth-v1 --dispute RD-0109   # withheld: above the cap
 125→python3 -m app.cli --pack ryde-synth-v1 --dispute RD-0108   # withheld: no deviation to measure
 126→```
 127→
 128→**Mock by default.** The default provider is a deterministic mock. Its free-text fields (claim
 129→summaries, arguments, the Judge's explanation) are prefixed `MOCK`; actions, amounts, rule IDs and
 130→evidence refs are not. A mock run is a plumbing demonstration, never a real ruling. The real model is
 131→Tencent Cloud ADP, one app per agent: put the three app keys in `.env` (see `.env.example`), then
 132→run `python3 -m app.server --llm tencent` or `python3 -m app.cli --llm tencent --dispute <id>`.
 133→
 134→## How this was built
 135→
 136→The code in `app/` and `ui/` was written in Tencent Cloud CodeBuddy. A planning agent wrote each
 137→session's brief and its failing tests first; CodeBuddy built until they passed, and the result was
 138→re-checked by running it, not by describing it. The screenshots in `evidence/` record those
 139→sessions as they happened.
 140→

 211→    category: str

 226→    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ serialisation
 227→
 228→    def to_dict(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
 229→        return asdict(self)
 230→
 231→    # --------------------------------------------------------------- citation surface
 232→
 233→    def field_refs(self) -> List[str]:
 234→        """Every legal citation, as dotted paths to the pack's computed scalars."""
 235→        refs: List[str] = []
 236→        _collect_refs(self.to_dict(), "", refs)
 237→        return sorted(refs)
 238→
 239→    def value_at(self, ref: str) -> Any:
 240→        """Resolve a dotted reference. Raises KeyError with the legal refs listed."""
 241→        node: Any = self.to_dict()
 242→        for part in ref.split("."):
 243→            if isinstance(node, dict) and part in node:
 244→                node = node[part]
 245→            elif isinstance(node, list) and part.isdigit() and int(part) < len(node):
 246→                node = node[int(part)]
 247→            else:
 248→                raise KeyError(
 249→                    "no evidence field %r in the pack for dispute %s" % (ref, self.dispute_id)
 250→                )
 251→        return node
 252→
 253→
 254→def _collect_refs(node: Any, prefix: str, out: List[str]) -> None:
 255→    if isinstance(node, dict):
 256→        for key, value in node.items():
 257→            if key in _NON_CITABLE_KEYS:
 258→                continue
 259→            _collect_refs(value, "%s.%s" % (prefix, key) if prefix else key, out)
 260→        return
 261→    if isinstance(node, list):
 262→        for index, value in enumerate(node):
 263→            _collect_refs(value, "%s.%d" % (prefix, index), out)
 264→        return
 265→    if node is None:
 266→        return
 267→    out.append(prefix)

I've read the brief, the policy RD-4 paragraph, the judge, the W28 target test and the six re-pinned files. I also verified my planned algorithm reproduces the brief's expected `provable_refund_sgd` table exactly on both packs (RD-0101 5.81 … RD-0109 55.16), and that the mock claims make exactly RD-0103/0105/0107 trip the new gate.

**Plan**

**1. `app/agents/judge.py` (the whole fix)**

- Constants beside `DE_MINIMIS_SGD`: `MATERIAL_DEVIATION_PCT = 20.0`, `MATERIAL_DEVIATION_KM = 1.0`, `MATERIAL_DEVIATION_GROSS_KM = 5.0`.
- New module-level `deviation_is_material(pack)`: `False` with no route block; `True` when `_is_figure(deviation_km) and deviation_km >= 5.0`, or when `_is_figure(deviation_pct) and _is_figure(deviation_km) and pct >= 20.0 and km >= 1.0`. Non-finite/bool/missing figures never qualify.
- New module-level `provable_refund_sgd(pack)`: max of `0.0`, a figure `difference_sgd`, `charged - component_sum` when `breakdown_consistent is False` and both figures, and `charged - recomputed_estimated_route_sgd` only when `deviation_is_material(pack)` and both figures. Never `deviation_fare_delta_sgd`. Returns `round(proven, 2)`, never below zero.
- Gate in `Judge.run` after the RD-5 `if/elif`, before `if not gate_failures:` — fires only for route-deviation cases with a non-`no action` ruling, no existing `ESC-2` entry, and no present-but-not-figure `difference_sgd`. A refund is held when `round(amount, 2) > provable_refund_sgd(pack)` (equal goes out); compensation is always held. Appends `("RD-4", reason)` and the exact summary `the ruling pays more than the records prove is owed (RD-4)`; refund reason carries both figures, compensation reason contains `driver`. Order becomes confidence, ESC-4, ESC-2, NS-6, RD-5, RD-4. Nothing rewrites the candidate.
- Update the module docstring ("four other gates" → five, naming RD-4) and the gates comment.

**2. `docs/architecture.md`**
- Overview paragraph: name RD-4 beside NS-6/RD-5 ("three money gates").
- Gates section: "Eight gates" → "Nine gates"; new RD-4 row after RD-5 naming `recomputed_estimated_route_sgd`, `difference_sgd`, `compensation`, file `app/agents/judge.py`.
- Mermaid gate node → `J --> G{"Gates pass? Confidence, cap, measured deviation, NS-6, RD-5, RD-4"}`.

**3. `README.md`**
- Same Mermaid node (blocks must stay identical).
- Gates paragraph under **Run**: "Five gates"/"all five" → "Six gates"/"all six", adding RD-4 (route refund larger than the records prove) while keeping `fare charged` inside the ESC-2 clause.

**4. Verify and commit**
- `/usr/bin/python3 -m unittest tests.test_w28_unproven_refunds` → green; full suite → 844 green.
- `python3 -m app.eval --llm mock` on both packs: confirm 11/18 and 10/17 decided, and that only RD-0103 (0.74), RD-0105 (5.56), RD-0107 (4.91) move to withheld by RD-4 — stop and report if anything else moves.
- Small commits once green. No live model, no edits under `tests/`, `tools/`, `data/`, `ui/` or `docs/policy.md`.

May I proceed?

def deviation_is_material(pack: EvidencePack) -> bool:
    """RD-1 in code: is the recorded route deviation material?

    Material at >= 5.0 km whatever the percentage, or at >= 20% and >= 1.0 km together.
    A missing, non-finite or bool figure is not material, and neither is a pack with no
    route block. When the gross distance limb is cleared the percentage is not needed at
    all — it may be missing.
    """
    route = pack.route
    if route is None:
        return False
    km = route.deviation_km
    if _is_figure(km) and km >= MATERIAL_DEVIATION_GROSS_KM:
        return True
    pct = route.deviation_pct
    return (
        _is_figure(km)
        and _is_figure(pct)
        and pct >= MATERIAL_DEVIATION_PCT
        and km >= MATERIAL_DEVIATION_KM
    )

    """RD-4: the largest refund the records actually prove the rider is owed.

    The max of three proofs, never below zero, rounded to the cent:

    1. ``fare.difference_sgd`` (RD-5, a pricing error);
    2. ``fare.charged_sgd - fare.component_sum_sgd`` when the breakdown is inconsistent
       (EV-3: the line items add up to less than the charge) — this works without rates;
    3. ``fare.charged_sgd - fare.recomputed_estimated_route_sgd`` when RD-1 says the
       deviation is material (RD-3 / RD-4: the charge above the fare the expected route
       would have cost).

        fare.breakdown_consistent is False
        and _is_figure(fare.charged_sgd)
        and _is_figure(fare.component_sum_sgd)
    ):
        proven = max(proven, fare.charged_sgd - fare.component_sum_sgd)
    if (
        deviation_is_material(pack)
        and _is_figure(fare.charged_sgd)
        and _is_figure(fare.recomputed_estimated_route_sgd)
    ):
